scenario.resume_intake_note: The upload step is represented by loading the synthetic JSON fixture. The repository has no upload endpoint, and its PDF/DOCX parser output is not directly connected to the ATS resume schema.

hr_interview.scoring_note: Uses the current Day 45 deterministic demonstration heuristics; the interview responses are synthetic.

technical_interview.score_source: illustrative rubric inputs from the simulation fixture

unified_score.note: Screening score was divided by 10 at the integration boundary because the unified config expects 0-10, while screening emits 0-100.

review_rules: Synthetic simulation requires human review before any real hiring action.

reasons: Synthetic simulation requires human review before any real hiring action.

candidate_level_summary.final_decision_comparison_note: The AI Hold / Review outcome was triggered by an explicit simulation human-review rule, not by a candidate-specific rejection threshold. The human decision to advance therefore differs in process state, not necessarily candidate assessment.

performance.measurement_note: One local synthetic run using a cached model; local model initialization is included but first-time model download is excluded. This is not a production load or throughput benchmark.

limitations: This is one local synthetic candidate run. Timings do not establish production throughput, reliability, or fairness.
Resume intake used an embedded JSON fixture; there is no production file-upload path or parser-to-ATS adapter in this run.
The HR transcript used synthetic answers assigned sequentially to adaptive questions; several prompt-answer pairs were mismatched, making the AI HR score provisional.
Technical interview flow was exercised, but its AI score came from illustrative rubric values rather than evaluation of free-text answers. The human rating used a synthetic answer sheet.
Human review reflects one reviewer who had access to simulation results; the comparison was not blinded or a multi-reviewer validation.
The separate screening intent/action benchmark covers 10 existing labeled cases only; its 100% agreement does not demonstrate broad accuracy.

ratings.note: Provisional: scripted answers were paired with mismatched adaptive questions.
Illustrative: human reviewed synthetic sample answers; engine score used rubric inputs.

final_decision.rationale: The user indicated that all human reviews are okay; recorded as approval to advance.

human_review.interpretation_note: The human ratings were supplied after the simulation results were discussed; this was not a blinded evaluation.
human_review.comparison_assessment: ATS and screening ratings closely align. HR comparison is provisional because prompt-answer pairs were mismatched. Technical comparison is illustrative because the interview engine did not evaluate the sample free-text answers.

findings.finding: A fixed synthetic answer list was fed sequentially into adaptive interview questions, so several answers did not address the question asked.
findings.example: The notice-period question received an answer about improving backend skills.
findings.impact: The HR score and its comparison with the human 90/100 rating are provisional and should not be treated as reliable candidate-level evaluation.

findings.finding: The question flow accepted placeholder answer-quality values; the engine did not score free-text responses.
findings.impact: The AI 81.5 score came from illustrative rubric inputs. The human 82 rating reviewed a synthetic sample answer set, so this is illustrative rather than a direct score comparison.

findings.finding: Screening emits a 0–100 score while unified scoring expects 0–10.
findings.impact: The simulation divides the screening score by 10 at the integration boundary; score scales should be standardized across modules.

findings.finding: The run loads a structured JSON fixture rather than exercising a real upload and parser-to-ATS path.
findings.impact: Resume ingestion and schema integration remain unvalidated end-to-end.

recommendations: Pair each HR response with the adaptive question it answers, persist the transcript, and reject or clarify off-topic responses before scoring.
Score actual technical free-text answers against a transparent rubric; retain the questions, answers, and rubric evidence for human review.
Standardize stage score ranges and validation at module boundaries instead of relying on an implicit divide-by-10 conversion.
Connect real PDF/DOCX upload and parser output to the ATS schema, then run tests using representative resumes and jobs.
Expand human evaluation beyond one synthetic candidate and 10 screening intent cases; assess agreement, fairness, and performance across a representative dataset.
